configKeys.effect: Bonus loot rolled in addition to the mob's normal death loot when an Enhanced AI "leader" mob dies. Format item_id;weight;min_count;max_count. It is one loot pool with exactly one roll, so precisely one entry is picked per leader kill, weighted; weights are relative and need not sum to 100 (the defaults happen to sum to 100, which is why the doc's 50/49/1 percentages read as literal chances). Count is a uniform range between min_count and max_count.
configKeys.range: no spec range; per-entry validator (EnhancedAiLeaderLootConfig.java:35-52) requires exactly 4 semicolon-separated parts, a parsable ResourceLocation, weight >= 1, min_count >= 1 and max_count >= min_count. It does NOT check that the item exists - an unknown id passes validation and is dropped later by the parser (EnhancedAiLeaderLootModule.java:79-85).

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.LootTableLoadEvent (EnhancedAiLeaderLootModule.java:56-62, @SubscribeEvent on the instance registered to NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize, lines 52-54; the body returns unless isModuleEnabled() and event.getName() equals enhancedai:leader_mob, then replaces the table via event.setTable) - the module's only event handler. NeoForge fires this event on the main event bus on the logical SERVER only, whenever server resources are loaded or reloaded.
notes:
DOC-WRITER NOTES (every point re-verified against the current working tree; line numbers are from it).

SOURCE FILES - exactly two, nothing else in the repo belongs to this module:
- src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/enhanced_ai_leader_loot/EnhancedAiLeaderLootModule.java (98 lines)
- src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/enhanced_ai_leader_loot/config/EnhancedAiLeaderLootConfig.java (60 lines)
No mixin package (src/main/java/.../mixin/ has no enhanced_ai_leader_loot dir, vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json has no entry), no standalone entry point (src/main/java/.../standalone/ has no enhanced_ai_leader_loot dir), no assets, no data files, no DeferredRegister, no Commands.literal, no KeyMapping. Doc page: docs/modules/enhanced_ai_leader_loot.md (staged rename from docs/enhanced_ai_leader_loot.md - the module javadoc line 30 and CLAUDE.md:94 still point at the old path). README paragraph: README.md:63-64.

HOW IT WORKS (provable): Enhanced AI rolls a separate loot table, enhancedai:leader_mob, for leader mobs in addition to their normal death loot and ships it empty as an extension point. onInitialize (Module.java:52-54) does nothing but NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this). onLootTableLoad (Module.java:56-62) returns unless isModuleEnabled() AND event.getName().equals(ResourceLocation enhancedai:leader_mob) (constant at line 35-36), then calls event.setTable(buildLeaderLootTable()). No Enhanced AI class is referenced anywhere in the module, so there is no compile-time dependency - only the ModList gate. (Module javadoc lines 22-30; docs page section "How this module hooks it".)

SIDE IS SERVER - PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED: the module registers its listener on both physical sides, but LootTableLoadEvent's own javadoc says it "is fired on the main Forge event bus, only on the logical server" and "is fired whenever server resources are loaded or reloaded" (decompiled NeoForge source net/neoforged/neoforge/event/LootTableLoadEvent.java in the Gradle cache - outside this repo, but it is the dependency this module compiles against). The module has no client code, no renderer, no packet, no keybind, no lang key, so nothing is client-side.

ALWAYS DROPS SOMETHING (with any non-empty valid config): the pool is LootPool.lootPool().setRolls(ConstantValue.exactly(1)) (Module.java:65) with no when(...) condition, so every leader kill yields exactly one of the surviving entries - there is no "nothing" outcome. With the default weights 50/49/1 (sum 100) the doc table's percentages happen to be literal chances; change any weight and the percentages shift, because weights are relative, not absolute. The table is built with LootContextParamSets.ENTITY (Module.java:96), matching the ENTITY param set Enhanced AI rolls it with.

EMPTY POOL - the previous fact sheet left this open, it is now settled: LootPool.Builder.build() accepts zero entries (no validation), and at runtime LootPool.addRandomItem guards the pick with `if (mutableint.intValue() != 0 && i != 0)`, so a pool with no entries silently produces nothing and does not throw. An all-invalid config therefore means leaders drop only their normal loot; it does NOT crash. Evidence: decompiled Minecraft source net/minecraft/world/level/storage/loot/LootPool.java in the Gradle cache (addRandomItem ~line 67-96, Builder.build ~line 235). That file is outside this repository - strong evidence, but not repo-internal; if the doc states it, state it as observed behaviour of the MC version we build against (1.21.1).

SILENT SKIP CONTRADICTS THE DOCS: docs/modules/enhanced_ai_leader_loot.md says "Invalid entries are skipped and logged". In code a malformed entry with parts.length != 4 is skipped with NO log at all (Module.java:69-71); an unknown item id logs a warn ONLY when debug logging is on (`if (getConfig().shouldDebugLog())`, Module.java:81-83); only a thrown exception during parsing is logged unconditionally, at ERROR (Module.java:91-93). A doc writer must not promise visible feedback for bad entries.

VALIDATOR vs PARSER - correcting the previous sheet's framing: the defineList validator (Config.java:35-52) checks 4 semicolon parts, a parsable ResourceLocation, weight >= 1, min_count >= 1 and max_count >= min_count, but it does NOT check that the item exists in the registry. So the parser's "item not found -> skip" branch (Module.java:79-85) is fully live and is the skip path a player will actually hit (typo, or an id from a mod that is not installed). Only the parts.length branch is a second safety net. Note also that String.split(";") drops trailing empty fields, so "minecraft:golden_carrot;50;6;" yields 3 parts and is rejected by both validator and parser.

UNKNOWN ITEM == AIR: BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId) returns Items.AIR for an unregistered id and the code treats item == Items.AIR as "not found" (Module.java:79-85). Consequence: minecraft:air can never be configured as a drop, and item ids from mods that are not loaded silently vanish from the pool.

CONFIG LOCATION AND THE TWO KEYS NOT LISTED HERE: leader_bonus_loot lives in section [modules.enhanced_ai_leader_loot] of the bundle's COMMON config (ModulesConfig.buildConfig pushes "modules", each module pushes its own id - AbstractModuleConfig.java:50-74; the spec is registered at VanillaPlusAdditions.java:131). Every module also gets "enabled" (default = module.isEnabledByDefault()) and "debug_logging" (enum AUTO/ON/OFF, default AUTO) from AbstractModuleConfig.java:58-66; those are framework-wide and are deliberately not listed in configKeys.

ENABLED BY DEFAULT: the module does not override isEnabledByDefault(); the interface default returns true (Module.java:73-75), so "enabled" defaults to true. It is still inert without Enhanced AI, because shouldInitialize() gates the whole initialization.

RELOAD SEMANTICS: isModuleEnabled() is checked only inside the LootTableLoadEvent handler, i.e. at loot-table load time, and the event only fires when server resources load or reload. Editing leader_bonus_loot, toggling "enabled", or using the core command /vpa module enable|disable enhanced_ai_leader_loot (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:239-268, runtime override resolved in ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled, ModuleManager.java:205-208) therefore has no effect until /reload or a world rejoin - and a table replaced earlier stays replaced until then.

NO STANDALONE JAR: build.gradle's standaloneModules list (lines 386-465, 39 entries) does not contain enhanced_ai_leader_loot; `grep -c enhanced_ai_leader_loot build.gradle` = 0, and there is no standalone/enhanced_ai_leader_loot package. It ships only inside the bundle jar, registered unconditionally at VanillaPlusAdditions.java:189 (registerModule always runs; only initialize() is gated).

NO LANG KEYS: grep -i for "enhanced" and "leader" in src/main/resources/assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/en_us.json returns nothing. Nothing user-visible beyond the config comments (Config.java:29-33) - no commands, no keybinds, no screens; all log strings are hardcoded English.

NO CHANGELOG ENTRY: grep -i "leader" in CHANGELOG.md finds nothing. The only "enhancedai" lines there (486, 558) belong to the hostile_endermen module's TeleportAntiCheeseMixin. The module arrived inside the multi-feature commit c309098 (2026-08-29, "Add tipped arrows from potions, netherite recipe rework, pathfinder quills, leader loot, egg stacking"), which is why it has no changelog line of its own.

DEFAULT COUNTS WERE RAISED ONCE - AFTER the first release: only two commits ever touched the module directory. c309098 added it (shipped in v1.0.0-beta.73) with golden_carrot 3-9 and golden_apple 1-3; 8654686 (2026-09-03, "Increase Enhanced AI leader bonus loot counts (#2)") raised them to 6-12 and 3-9 and landed in v1.0.0-beta.74 (git describe --contains 8654686 -> v1.0.0-beta.74~4). The enchanted golden apple entry (1;1;1) was never changed. So beta.73 screenshots showing smaller counts are correct for beta.73 - the current defaults are the raised ones.

REFERENCE VERSION: scripts/docgen/data/tested-versions.json pins "enhancedai": "4.2.2.1"; the doc page states the leader mechanism (LEADER flag, LootContextParamSets.ENTITY, the empty data/enhancedai/loot_table/leader_mob.json) was read out of `javap -c` on exactly that jar. Which mobs can become leaders (#enhancedai:overworld_zombies = Zombie, Drowned, Giant, Husk, Zombie Villager; #enhancedai:overworld_skeletons = Skeleton, Stray, Bogged) comes from Enhanced AI, is documented only in docs/modules/enhanced_ai_leader_loot.md and is NOT verifiable from this repository.

NO DEPENDENCY DECLARATION: "enhancedai" does not appear anywhere in src/main/resources (neoforge.mods.toml included), so the gate is purely runtime - as intended, but nothing warns a player that the module is inert without Enhanced AI.
oneLiner: Every banner-carrying "leader" mob from the Enhanced AI mod drops a handful of golden carrots (6-12) or golden apples (3-9) when you kill it - and, at a 1% chance, a single enchanted golden apple - on top of its normal loot; exactly one of those entries drops per leader, and the whole table is a single weighted config list you can rewrite.

requiredMods.evidence: EnhancedAiLeaderLootModule.java:46-49 - `protected boolean shouldInitialize() { return ModList.get().isLoaded("enhancedai"); }`. AbstractModule.initialize (AbstractModule.java:90-105) logs "Module '{}' is disabled and will not be initialized" and returns at lines 96-99 before onInitialize(), so without Enhanced AI the event handler is never registered. Not declared in META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml - runtime gate only.
requiredMods.whatItAdds: Enhanced AI's "Leaders" feature promotes random Zombie-/Skeleton-family mobs to banner-carrying leaders and rolls the separate, deliberately empty loot table enhancedai:leader_mob for them on death. Without Enhanced AI there are no leaders and that table does not exist, so the module has nothing to hook and stays completely inert (the module is still registered and still shows up in config and /vpa module status).

shortDescription: Adds bonus golden food loot to Enhanced AI's banner-carrying leader mobs.
